scope: Submission exemption/reference policy validation, consistent Pages display, and semantic topological-order sample checking

policy.origin: Root added submission_policy/submission_action and SHA-bound user-authorized documentation_only rules. This follow-up hardens parsing and adds regression coverage.
policy.documentation_only: Exemption applies only to its exact current full-source SHA. Implementation changes and even Submission-annotation byte changes invalidate it. It changes submission_required/queue stage only, never source-match evidence or current_ac.
policy.reference: Known, unique, nonself replacements are required; all must be direct non-reference primaries. This intentionally rejects reference chains as well as cycles. Historical status/evidence stay unchanged; old reference IDs do not enter either queue mode.
hardening: Strict integer format=1 (bool is not accepted).
Duplicate JSON keys, duplicate/unknown/invalid-type IDs, missing reason, unknown kind and invalid source SHA fail closed.
Reference replacement lists must exist and contain valid, unique, nonself IDs.
Action output copies replacement lists and accepts hexadecimal SHA case consistently.
tests: Absent/empty policy preserves default status and queue behavior.
Exact-SHA exemption never creates AC or rewrites recorded submitted SHA/history.
New implementation byte changes reactivate resubmission; no normalized-source alias is used for the exemption.
Reference entries retain historical status but are excluded from queues; unsubmitted replacement remains pending.
Readme/status and Pages distinguish exemption/reference from current AC.

pages.change: Only online_table status-label selection and two tests were added; other existing Pages work is preserved.
labels: 説明変更のみ・再提出不要
参考検証・移行先あり
pages.nonpromotion: Old [AC] remains in the separate submission-result column, while current status stays source_changed. Rendering does not mutate the entry; unknown policy kinds keep default labels.
pages.scope: No Pages site was generated or published by this follow-up.

topological_checker.name: topological_order
topological_checker.compatibility: Legacy topological mode delegates to the same checker.
topological_checker.semantics: Exactly N ASCII integer tokens forming a complete0..N-1 permutation, and position[u]<position[v] for every one of M declared edges. All valid orders are accepted.
topological_checker.input_validation: Checks exact edge count, vertex bounds, missing/duplicate IDs, malformed/underscore/Unicode/float tokens, extra output, cycles and self-loops. Signed decimal spellings are parsed as integers; negative vertices are rejected by bounds.
topological_checker.complexity: O(V+E) time and O(V+E) parsed input/output storage.
topological_checker.independent_oracle: Kahn-style exhaustive branch enumeration, rather than the checker position-map algorithm.
topological_checker.cpp_integration: Four GCC15.2/Clang21 checked/skip candidate-driver builds;20 cases (official, alternative-order, isolated vertices and100000-vertex chain/fan) semantically passed.
topological_checker.candidate_disposition: The AOJ driver is no longer adopted under final priority LC→Yukicoder→AtCoder→AOJ. Its pre-compatibility-change snapshots remain only integration-test evidence; no online AC or active-target claim.

validation.unrelated_changes: None to public libraries/mains, live policy JSON, generated source, live status/Readme/journal or commit state by this follow-up. Test fixtures write only temporary repositories. Root owns global generation and final live policy edits.
validation.compatibility_experiment: Abandoned GCC11/std::unreachable exploratory checks are stored separately in a private ignored archive and are excluded from these public result totals.
